source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    To Select Operations > Factory Reset and Reset BMC and server settings.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Set BMC to factory without error.
2. BMC setting should change to default setting after BMC back.
In addition to server settings, this option resets BMC settings, including: all BMC account data, all changed passwords, all policies, LDAP configurations, network addresses, and time of day.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" mc reset cold 2>&1; sleep 5; echo "--- factory-restore via Redfish (destructive) ---"; curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -X POST https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/Actions/Manager.Reset -d '{"ResetType":"FactoryReset"}' -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n"
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: perform a factory reset of the BMC (method shown) and then confirm the BMC returns to defaults and the BMC-IP becomes reachable again after restart.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: DESTRUCTIVE: factory-resets the BMC, erasing all users/settings/IP config and restoring defaults; requires physical/console recovery if network config is lost. Confirm with user and ensure the operator can recover access before running.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL correctly flags destructive loss of access, but the proposed sequence first cold-resets the BMC, waits only five seconds, then sends an unverified `FactoryReset` value to a generic Manager.Reset endpoint using insecure TLS and exposed credentials. Reachability alone does not prove defaults or server-setting scope.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly rejects the generic sequence and requires vendor reset-scope confirmation, secure full baseline, one approved action, independent recovery and complete default comparison. V3.1 further separates reset action, BMC recovery phases, bootstrap access and any post-verdict reconfiguration.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 911/2291 accepts the command as conditionally runnable but does not validate whether the action exists, distinguish cold reset from factory reset, secure credentials/TLS, preserve evidence before log loss, define defaults or prove recovery after IP/account changes.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: Ordinary BMC warm/cold reboot, network-default, user-delete and firmware-update cases are not equivalent to a full factory reset. A successful BMC ping or `mc info` cannot establish reset scope.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1073, Wistron-BMC-00202-V003 or edd365d3bb786465 draft exists in the invalidated run.
historical_reviews.v3: No V3 overlay exists for this exact case.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves the source WebUI Operations path and listed settings; ED-34 treats default matrix, recovery and supported action as Project inputs; ED-35 preserves destructive functional coverage rather than replacing it with a read-only version check; ED-38 forbids execution without point-of-action approval, automatic retry or an engineer verdict.

original_test_intent: Verify one approved BMC factory-reset operation restores the documented BMC and in-scope server settings to their authoritative defaults, removes the listed account, credential, policy, directory, network and time customizations, and permits controlled secure recovery.
original_method: Securely baseline/export all in-scope BMC/server configuration and preserved logs, confirm the exact vendor-supported Operations > Factory Reset action and default matrix, arrange an independent physical/discovery/bootstrap recovery path, execute the approved action once, observe bounded recovery, regain access securely and compare every in-scope post-reset value before any approved reconfiguration.
manual_activity: An engineer confirms destructive scope, authoritative defaults, recovery/bootstrap route, maintenance window and the exact WebUI action. A human must provide point-of-action confirmation and retain physical or independent recovery control. Automation may export/redact baselines, monitor staged recovery and compare configuration, but cannot authorize, repeat or judge the reset.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT identity, firmware/build/active bank, host state and current network/access paths
Vendor documentation for the exact factory-reset action, BMC/server-setting scope, preserved exceptions and reset/power behavior
Authoritative default-value matrix across accounts, policies, directory, network/VLAN, time/NTP, certificates, alerting, thresholds, boot and other server settings
Secure configuration export, hashes, secret-handling and preserved pre-reset audit/SEL evidence
Factory network discovery/default IP and approved initial-account or zero-touch provisioning procedure
Independent physical/console recovery, owner/vendor escalation and bounded recovery deadlines
Maintenance/change approval, proof no conflicting OOB/host work is active and separately approved post-verdict reconfiguration
safety_requirements: Treat the action as destructive and target-specific; verify asset, MAC/serial, firmware and host state through an independent path immediately before confirmation.
Do not clear logs. Export and preserve configuration, audit/SEL and recovery artifacts before the reset because the action may erase them.
Do not run the DeepSeek cold-reset-plus-generic-Redfish sequence, use `curl -k`, expose passwords on command lines or assume `FactoryReset` is a supported Manager.Reset value.
Confirm physical/discovery/bootstrap access and recovery ownership before losing accounts, addresses, certificates and directory authentication.
Execute one approved factory reset only; do not issue a preliminary cold reset, automatic retry, host power cycle or guessed fallback while recovery is pending.

Record defaults before reconfiguration. Stop/escalate on wrong scope, unexpected host impact, identity change, recovery timeout or insecure bootstrap; restore only after verdict evidence is preserved.
agent_execution_scope: Validate identity, supported action/scope, default matrix, secure baseline, bootstrap/recovery and absence of conflicting operations; present the exact destructive action for explicit human confirmation.
After approval and human WebUI invocation, timestamp disconnect and bounded network, management-service, discovery/bootstrap, authentication and full-sensor recovery phases from an independent path.
Collect post-reset configuration and compare every defined BMC/server setting against authoritative defaults, distinguishing preserved/exempt, volatile and secret fields.
Archive evidence before any approved reconfiguration and stop without log clear, additional reset, insecure credential handling, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the source WebUI factory-reset control, exact destructive scope, default/exemption matrix, host impact and maintenance window.
Approve secure baseline/export, bootstrap credentials/provisioning, independent recovery and non-return escalation plan.
Confirm one action, supervise recovery, review complete default and host-state evidence, issue the formal verdict and only then authorize reconfiguration.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unsafe and technically unproven: a cold reset is not a factory reset; the generic Redfish action/value may be unsupported; five seconds is not a recovery contract; insecure TLS and command-line passwords are unacceptable; an HTTP response or reachability cannot prove defaults.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the exact vendor-documented Operations > Factory Reset action once after destructive confirmation. A supported API/OEM override may be used only with its action URI/allowable values, TLS/authentication and scope verified against the target firmware.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Operations > Factory Reset wording, inclusion of BMC and server settings, listed accounts/passwords/policies/LDAP/network/time fields, no Script, DeepSeek command/risk and 10/10-minute estimates remain preserved; Review does not claim those ten minutes are a recovery deadline.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Capture a secure complete baseline, confirm vendor factory scope/defaults and recovery, execute the source WebUI action once, recover through an independent approved route and compare the entire default matrix before reconfiguration.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC firmware/WebUI and chassis/server-setting integration with verified recovery access.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware/build/active bank, WebUI/API schema, board/BIOS/CPLD revisions, configuration schema and provisioning versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: BMC vendor factory-reset and default-setting specification, Project provisioning/security baseline and physical recovery SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact scope/defaults, secure evidence, one-shot approval, staged recovery and bootstrap/reconfiguration separation while retaining the destructive WebUI purpose.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A generic API or cold reset does not prove the WebUI factory-reset path; reachability does not prove configuration defaults; restoring a backup before comparison destroys default-state evidence.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Supported action, default matrix, secure export, bootstrap/recovery, approval and deadlines.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The test intentionally destroys management configuration and may strand access or alter host/server behavior; default credentials or insecure recovery can create a security incident.

project_override_considerations: A Project may approve a documented Redfish/OEM/vendor-tool factory-reset action only if the original WebUI method, actual action URI/value, firmware support, reason, engineering approval, exact destructive scope and equivalent default/recovery coverage are recorded. Passing the override does not claim the WebUI control passed. A normal BMC reset is not an equivalent override.
expected_evidence: Approval/change record, target asset/MAC/serial/firmware/host state, vendor action/scope reference and no-conflicting-operation check
Secure redacted configuration export/hash and pre-reset matrix for all listed and Project-defined BMC/server settings plus preserved audit/SEL
WebUI action screenshots/audit or documented approved override, single-action proof and staged disconnect/recovery/bootstrap timeline
Post-reset identity, firmware, host state and complete authoritative default comparison with preserved/exempt/volatile/secret distinctions
Physical/discovery/bootstrap recovery proof, no retry/insecure credential use, evidence captured before reconfiguration, final disposition and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Title, Procedure and Criteria consistently require a factory reset and explicitly include BMC plus server settings. The exact supported action, default values and scope boundaries are materially missing but are Project/vendor readiness inputs rather than competing source purposes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The destructive factory-reset objective is clear. A Project can supply vendor action/scope, default matrix, secure baseline and recovery. Until then execution is not ready, but the review is complete and not permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains PACKAGE but rejects its unsafe combined reset sequence, insecure TLS/credentials and reachability-only evidence; requires one supported action and full default/recovery proof.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on critical destructive controls and adds explicit separation of reset, bootstrap recovery, evidence-before-reconfiguration and host/server-scope verification.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-exists sanity with firmware-specific action validation, complete default matrix and one-shot recovery contract.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Keeps ordinary reboot, network/user reset and firmware actions non-equivalent.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents a normal cold reset plus an unsupported insecure API call from being treated as a factory reset, and prevents mere network return from being reported as proof that all destructive defaults and server settings are correct.
independent_technical_reasoning: Factory reset is a configuration-domain operation, not a reset type that can be inferred from a generic Manager.Reset endpoint. Implementations vary in what they erase or preserve and can change network and credentials before remote evidence is collected. The test is valid only with a version-specific scope/default matrix, evidence captured before loss, independent bootstrap/recovery and a single approved action followed by comparison before restoration.
